body:
From: Pyro <Valderrey@email.msn.com>

> (re: leftists)
> ..... today they have virtually all the institutions under their
> grip, and thus cannot really be deemed as iconoclasts, generally.

   TK's activities, and the Manifesto that supposedly justified them,
 occured during right-wing White-House administrations with the
 singular exception of Jimmy Carter.  Therefore, perceptions which
 want to claim reference to today's circumstances cannot in general
 be contemporaneous with the political background of his Manifesto.


   [ ... ]

> 7. The projection of liberals is particularly evident.  In reality, PC
> is reverse McCarthyism; yet they accuse people who refer to them as
> "PC" to be continuing the legacy of McCarthy.  The reality is, PC is a
> term which can be defined, although not easily -- and is used by them
> to smear opponents in a similar way McCarthy did.  By referring to
> them as PC you are not _aiming_ to smear, but are pointing out that
> they are smearing you.  If that makes them feel self-conscious, they
> started it.

    What is "reverse McCarthyism?"  In what sense is the "non-PC'er"
  smeared when you've said that they are -not- "automatically right?"


  [ ... ]

> When TK referred to conservatives as fools, it
> was because of their focus on economic growth at the expense of social
> stability.  TK's criticism was not directed toward their social
> policies, but at their _economic_ideals_.  PC'ers are not so much
> concerned with economics as they are in meddling into people's
> personal affairs.  So, as you can see, that speck of criticism
> against conservatives has been greatly misinterpreted.

   Closer examination of TK's actual words reveals your misreading.
 His criticism addressed the -side-effects- of unintended consequences
 engendered by conservative support for "technological progress and
 economic growth ... causing rapid changes in all _other_ aspects of
 a society ... [which] inevitably break down traditional _values_."
 Those remarks aren't directly addressing conservative _economic_ideals_
 which incidentally coincided with that "technological progress and
 economic growth" TK criticized -elsewhere- in the Manifesto, but the
 "other aspects" such as disintegration of "traditional values," that
 are constituent impacts upon _social_ policies.  Could you manage to
 elaborate on where such "misinterpretation" really occurs?  You have
 offered the definition/characterization of "PC" as a condition of
 being "automatically right."  Continuing to run with your definition,
 doesn't it necessarily follow that meddling by those who are granted
 "automatic rights" to do so, is also "automatically right?"  Or were
 you about to say that "PC" means something other than the state of
 being "automatically right?"  More clarification, please.

        "50. The conservatives are fools: They whine about the decay
         of traditional values, yet they enthusiastically support
         technological progress and economic growth. Apparently it
         never occurs to them that you can't make rapid, drastic
         changes in the technology and the economy of a society with
         out causing rapid changes in all other aspects of the society
         as well, and that such rapid changes inevitably break down
         traditional values."



           - regards
           - jb
